body:
Update: I found a workaround. If I enable Khronos OpenXR plugin instead of Magic Leap and enable HTC Vendor - it suddenly works, because the openxr vendors plugin adds the relevant project setting in this case.
So maybe this is a bug for the vendors plugin and not the engine itself.

> [@m4gr3d](https://github.com/m4gr3d) [@BastiaanOlij](https://github.com/BastiaanOlij) Do you guys remember why we have this?

We have this because each and every Android platform is deciding on their own permissions for this feature. In order to ensure code is not run until this permission is given, we've had to introduce a feature flag to switch the logic.

So for each and every vendor we have to add code to the vendor plugin, including vendors that don't require a permission and just need to set the feature flag. HTC falls under this last category which is why it functions as a workaround, ML obviously we didn't add the needed code. But using the HTC export means you miss out on all the ML specific stuff.

We thus have to add the same bit of code to the ML export.

As you know, this is one of the areas I'm fighting hard for to change, it is completely nullifying the effectiveness of a standard here. But it's something that seems to be the norm on AOSP and is thus unlikely to change. We're likely going to introduce more of this.

> So for each and every vendor we have to add code to the vendor plugin, including vendors that don't require a permission and just need to set the feature flag.

But why do we do the check for the feature tag in Godot itself? Can't we just handle all the Android permission stuff in the vendor plugin?

I feel like if OpenXR advertises the extension, and the project setting is enabled, then within Godot we should just try to use it. If the vendor plugin doesn't do the permission stuff, it won't work, but that's like all extensions that need a permission - why does this one in particular have this extra feature tag check within Godot?

> But why do we do the check for the feature tag in Godot itself? Can't we just handle all the Android permission stuff in the vendor plugin?

We do, the android permission stuff is checked on the vendor side

BUT skipping over the needed steps for the eye gaze interaction is something we need to do in core.

The feature flag is just how we communicate from the vendor extension, to core, that the permission is given, as the permission hasn't been standardised and the core has no other way of checking.

We'll likely need to add something similar in due time for spatial entities.

> The feature flag is just how we communicate from the vendor extension, to core, that the permission is given, as the permission hasn't been standardised and the core has no other way of checking.

Just to clarify, I think that the permission string **PERMISSION_XR_EXT_eye_gaze_interaction** is working, but the feature for extension itself **XR_EXT_EYE_GAZE_INTERACTION_EXTENSION_NAME** isn't. It is supposedly something different from a permission check. At least check for the supported permission wasn't the one that failed.

@dsnopek it's worth trying, but it's too long ago to remember exactly where things didn't gel.

Like I said, the eye interaction API was designed before anything around Android was added to the spec and nobody knew how these permissions systems would work or that this would even be introduced. The API is from all the way back in 2020, the Quest Pro, the first AOSP device with eye tracking, wasn't introduced until 2022.

I vaguely remember its the `xrSyncActions` that was misbehaving if eye tracking was enabled and the eye gaze interaction was part of the action map but no permission was given. And it wasn't that we got an error, it was the internal systems filling logcat with permission errors.

That said, this was years ago, that behaviour may have changed.

I'd like @m4gr3d to weigh in though, he came up with the feature system to drive this so he may remember other factors that are at play here.
